_doc: CDD engine contract lexicon — the single vocabulary source for the command contract (C6): the status-value vocab plus its dual-axis mapping, the stdout contract tokens (capsule + route anchors + the banned old-shape names + the read-back annotation the review fix `next:` line carries), the G2 residue ban table, the zero-debt domains (the escape-directive ban, the prebuilt-module source-plane residue, the review buildability dual-evidence wording), and the skill-anatomy schema reference. The read-back annotation and the zero-debt vocabulary are single-sourced here and on the engine command output, and the orchestrator skill surface carries zero literal restates. The harness contract data (rows / markers / refs) lives in the engine harness contract (config/harness-contract.json — the unique harness contract, C8); this file keeps the pure word tables. Ships to consumers via the build mirror entry (dist/config/contract-lexicon.json, same pipeline and cadence as the harness contract).

escape.wording: the escape-directive ban — the two TypeScript escape directives settle to zero across the zero-debt source faces (engine src · scripts · kairos tests · the config planes) and stay fully banned: any re-appearance fails the guard; the docs face is covered by the live-face grep gate

zeroDebt.wording: the zero-debt source plane — the repository source faces carry zero prebuilt-module files: the plane is fully typed (.ts), the product build emits under dist/ (excluded from the zero-debt faces), and the orchestrator skills keep zero literal restates of the zero-debt vocabulary

buildability.dualEvidence: Buildability dual-evidence — the reviewer explicitly runs the repository's typecheck command (tsc --noEmit, or the repo equivalent) AND its test command; a buildability finding asserts both commands ran (dual evidence, not a single check)
buildability.wording: the review buildability axis — findings carry dual-evidence self-reports (typecheck + test both executed); the wording renders command descriptions, never a toolchain literal
